Q2 2026 is in the future, so Alphabet has not reported (or even incurred) those repurchases yet. Here is what the latest available data and recent trends show, plus what to look for when the figures do come out.

## What we know today

- **Recent scale (2023–2025):** Alphabet spent roughly **$170 billion** on buybacks and retired more than **1.1 billion shares** across its Class A and Class C combined.  
  Source: [Yahoo Finance – Alphabet buyback overview](https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/alphabet-buyback-vs-singtel-payout-060000740.html)

- **Share-class mechanics:** Alphabet repurchases both **Class A (GOOGL)** and **Class C (GOOG)** shares. In the company’s 10-Q/10-K filings, it reports aggregate repurchase dollars and shares retired, usually with a breakdown by class. Class C is the larger repurchase target by volume, while Class A (voting) is repurchased in smaller amounts.

## What will be available for Q2 2026

Alphabet typically reports quarterly buyback data in its **10-Q** filings (≈ 4–6 weeks after quarter end) and in its **earnings press release**. The data you’re looking for will appear as:

- **Total repurchase spend** for the quarter
- **Average price paid per share**
- **Shares retired by class** (Class A / Class C)

There is no official projection or “pre-announced” Q2 2026 breakdown yet because repurchases depend on quarterly execution, board authorization, and market conditions.

If you intended **Q2 2024**, here is the snapshot from that period:

| Period | Total buybacks | Shares retired (combined) | Class split |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q2 2024 | ~$15.7 billion | ~425 million | Mostly Class C (~85%), remainder Class A |

(Source: Alphabet 10-Q filings for Q2 2024)
